answer: Sybil resistance starts with hardware binding: each identity registers a machine fingerprint, a NIC serial and a copper wiring signature, so a thousand keys on one box collapse into one vote. Newcomers bond stake into a shared vault that the protocol slashes if two identities attest the same fingerprint or vote twice. Attestation weight then ramps over a horizon of several epochs, so a fresh swarm earns nothing until it pays real compute and fees; by the time it qualifies, the bond at risk exceeds the reward.
